speaker: narrator
text: This is Mia. She is six, and tonight she is stuck on one small sound.

speaker: mia
text: Mmm.

speaker: narrator
text: Her teacher has a full classroom. Her nanay is still at work. And the signal at home is gone again.

speaker: narrator
text: So Mia closes the book.

speaker: narrator
text: Then someone small, with very big eyes, peeks in.

speaker: lily
text: Hi there! I'm so happy you're here. Let's play and learn together!

speaker: narrator
text: This is Lily, and this is PlayIT: a phonics game for Grade 1 learners. It follows DepEd's Marungko order, listens to the child, and works offline.

speaker: narrator
text: No Wi-Fi needed. Mia just taps her letter.

speaker: narrator
text: First, she hears it. Then she says it,

speaker: mia
text: Mouse!

speaker: narrator
text: and the phone itself checks her voice. Nothing leaves the device.

speaker: narrator
text: Miss it? Lily never scolds. She shows the mouth shape and says it with her.

speaker: narrator
text: Next, she finds the pictures that start with the sound. Then the letters blend into real words.

speaker: narrator
text: And parents get a plain progress report.

speaker: narrator
text: We tested with 30 people: 16 children, plus 5 parents and 9 teachers.

speaker: narrator
text: 15 of 16 children chose the happy face, and 14 of 16 would play it again.

speaker: narrator
text: The grown-ups who open the door? Parents gave it 4.6 for Grade 1 fit, 4.4 to recommend. Teachers scored teaching 4.7.

speaker: narrator
text: One teacher called it "very useful and engaging for Grade 1 learners."

speaker: narrator
text: No signal. No ads. No child left waiting for a turn.

speaker: narrator
text: Just a little tarsier, and one sound at a time.

speaker: narrator
text: We are Group 56 from CIT University, and this is PlayIT.

speaker: lily
text: Play it!
